scenes.say: What happens when new data for last week shows up today? How do you make sure your results stay accurate?

scenes.label: Late Data
scenes.sub: Data that arrives after its expected window.
scenes.say: Late-arriving data means information shows up after your pipeline already processed that time period.

rows.b: Find late records by date or ID

scenes.say: To handle late data, first detect it, then reprocess just the affected partitions, and finally upsert those records to keep things correct.

scenes.title: Reprocessing a Partition
scenes.say: For example, if new records for June first arrive late, you find them, reprocess that partition, and upsert into your table.

scenes.question: What if you ignore late-arriving data?
scenes.right: Your data will be incomplete or wrong. Always plan for late arrivals.
scenes.say: Here's a trap: If you ignore late-arriving data, your results will be incomplete or incorrect. Always plan to handle it.
